checks.label: The quadratic formula for ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is x = (−b ± √(b^2 − 4ac)) ÷ 2a: on every screen, and at every a, b and c tried on the handles, each root it gives makes the rule 0, and the roots drawn are exactly those

Completing the square converts ax^2 + bx + c to a(x + b/(2a))^2 + (c − b^2/(4a)): for every screen's rule and every a, b and c tried on the handles, the two agree at every x tried, and at each root the bracket squared is (b^2 − 4ac)/(4a^2)

The discriminant distinguishes two distinct real roots, one repeated real root, or non-real complex roots only: on every screen and setting tried, the picture draws two roots and two equal arrows when b² − 4ac is above zero, one root and arrows of no length at zero, and no roots or arrows below zero, and the readout says which
Both arrows start on the dashed axis at x = −b ÷ 2a and are equal, each √(b² − 4ac) ÷ 2a long (its size when a is negative), so the axis sits halfway between the roots, which average to −b ÷ 2a

On y = x² + 6x + c, raising c from 0 to 12 takes the readout 36 − 4c down by 4 each step, from 36 to −12; the arrows shrink every step, meet at x = −3 when c is 9, where the readout is 0, and from c = 10 there are none and it says no real roots

Every puzzle accepts only its right answer, worked out from its rule; each wrong pick of roots, put back into the rule, does not give 0 (or, dropping the ±, gives one root and misses the other) while the right ones do, and each hint quotes the rule's own value there

The worked numbers: 36 − 8 = 28 with arrows of 2.65 to −0.35 and −5.65; 36 − 20 = 16 with arrows of 2 to −1 and −5, where 1 and 5 give 12 and 60 and the slip's −4 and −8 give −3 and 21; √28 = 2√7, about 5.29; 16 + 48 = 64, not −32 or −64; 36 − 4c from 36 to −12; 4 − 20 = −16; 16 + 40 = 56 with arrows of 3.74; 144 − 144 = 0 at 1.5; 49 − 40 = 9; the firework's 204.49 + 392 = 596.49 with arrows of 2.49 to 3.95 and −1.03; 25 + 12 = 37 with roots 0.18 and −1.85; and the practice check −32.95 + 22.96 + 10 = 0.01 at x = 5.74

Before Check a puzzle hides the curve, the roots and b² − 4ac; after a right answer the curve is drawn whole with its axis, arrows and roots, and a wrong pick puts its own numbers back into the rule, in red
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
